method_note: Scale established per plate from the graduated metre bar ('Échelle de 0,01 c. pour mètre', 1:100). Tick x-positions read by pixel analysis (threshold darkness on the tick row), px/m taken from the longest unambiguous labelled span. Ground line = top of the pavement hatch / base of the piers, located from a 2x-4x crop. All heights measured upward from that line. Floor lines are taken at the TOP of each storey's crowning string-course / entablature corona, read off metre-gridded overlay crops rendered at 2-4x. Window heads/sills, door jambs and arch crowns read the same way. NO plate in this group carries a printed dimension callout, so every value here is a scale-bar measurement, not a printed figure.

plates.notes: Widest and tallest in the group: 16.9 m frontage, 7 regular bays at 2.23 m, 24.35 m to the roof top. The 2e étage is the tallest window (h/w 2.07), not the 1er. The comble is a big curved (bell-profile) mansard containing two full levels of accommodation and is 28% of total height — a strong counter-example to a single 'comble fill' constant.

cross_plate_observations: Storey taper is NOT a universal constant in this group. rue Neuve des Mathurins 39 tapers cleanly (0.89, 0.85, 0.74); Sébastopol 1 tapers moderately (0.86, 0.90); boulevard St-Germain 6 tapers once (0.84) then stops; boulevard de Sébastopol 120 does not taper at all (three étages at exactly 3.20 m). Range of the 2e/1er taper across the five well-behaved plates: 0.84 to 1.00.

Comble/total height ranges from 0.122 (Sébastopol 120) to 0.279 (Sébastopol 1). The high value is explained: that comble holds two habitable levels. Excluding it, the range is 0.122-0.219, median ~0.14.
Eaves height clusters tightly: 17.55, 18.15, 18.28, 19.05, 19.82, 19.98 m — all just under the 20 m facade limit of the 1859 decree. This is an external validation that the scale readings are right.

The door is the most consistent absolute in the group. Pedestrian entrance doors: 1.66, 1.80, 1.81, 1.91 m wide by 2.78-3.40 m high (h/w 1.64-1.89). Carriage arches (porte cochère): 2.57-2.59 m wide, 3.47 m (flat-arched) to 5.00 m (full arch) high.

Window opening width is remarkably constant WITHIN each building (1.14-1.36 m, identical on every storey of a given facade) and varies only modestly between buildings. Storey differentiation is done by window HEIGHT, i.e. by h/w, which ranges 1.14-2.19 across storeys.

Bay pitch ranges 2.09-3.06 m. Three plates are exactly regular (Mathurins 3.06, Sébastopol 1 2.23) and three are deliberately irregular, with the central bays either wider (rue Bergère) or narrower (rue du Conservatoire, St-Germain) than the flanking bays. A generator that assumes uniform pitch will be right about half the time.
bay pitch / facade width ranges 0.132 (7 bays) to 0.247 (4 bays) — it is essentially 1/n_bays plus edge margin, not an independent constant.
